subject: [Action requested] Finlytics: sudden throughput & tail-latency spike on model-3a-v2
messages:
From: Amelia Turner <amelia.turner@finlytics.com>
To: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Mar 2028 08:12:23 -0700
Subject: API errors & 500s — p95 jump since 07:45 PDT (model-3a-v2)

Ethan / team,

We started seeing a sharp increase in errors and long tail latency starting ~07:45 PDT this morning. User-facing errors are up (rate-limited 500s), and our instrumentation shows p95 for text-generation calls to model-3a-v2 jumped from ~180ms to ~1.1s. Total throughput remained roughly constant but timeouts spiked.

This is impacting a portion of our users on our billing endpoint; we need immediate mitigation. Can you confirm whether this is a known rollout or a canary gone wrong? We do not have the capacity to absorb prolonged degradation — our SLOs are at stake.

I've attached a short log extract and a screenshot of our Grafana panel.

Attachments: finlytics_error_log_0312.txt (text), p95-trends-3a-v2.png (png)

Thanks,
Amelia Turner
Head of Engineering Operations
Finlytics
From: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 12 Mar 2028 08:20:41 -0700
Subject: Re: API errors & 500s — p95 jump since 07:45 PDT (model-3a-v2)

Amelia — thanks for the heads up and the logs. We're looking into this now. Initial triage from monitoring: beginning 07:43 PDT we see a discrete increase in tail latency correlated with requests routed to model-3a-v2 on the hosted route for Finlytics (prod/us-west). No scheduled rollout on our side at that time.

Immediate proposed mitigations (we can action within 10–20m):
- Flip routing to model-3a-v1 (previous stable variant) for Finlytics via a routing override (soft fallback) and ramp to 100% if metrics return to baseline.
- Enable q8m quantized fallback variant for a subset of traffic (lower perf but reduced memory pressure).
- Open INF-9876 (tracking) and capture a postmortem; we'll share timelines.

We need a quick authorization to perform the routing override / temporary rollback and to apply a limited SLA carveout while we stabilize. If you approve, Marissa will confirm and we'll start.

I'll attach an internal latency snapshot and our initial read.

Attachments: internal-latency-analysis-ethan-20280312.pdf (pdf)

—Ethan
Ethan Park

Amelia — quick operational note: we can do the routing override now. For transparency, the steps we plan to execute within the next 30 minutes are:

1) Route 50% of Finlytics traffic to model-3a-v1 immediately, leave 50% on v2 for metric validation.
2) If p95 for both cohorts is < 300ms after 10 minutes, ramp to 100% v1.
3) If fallback to q8m is needed (memory pressure), we'll apply as a secondary measure.
4) Provide a one-page incident summary and a credit proposal within 24 hours.

Do you authorize us to proceed with those steps now? Also, is a quick 15m call helpful to coordinate?

—Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Mar 2028 08:33:55 -0700
Subject: Re: API errors & 500s — p95 jump since 07:45 PDT (model-3a-v2)

Quick technical readout — I've pulled traces from the service and correlated with node-level OOM/retry logs. Preliminary hypothesis: an inference runtime kernel selection change introduced in the v2 build interacts poorly with longer sequence lengths that Finlytics sends (avg seq ~1.8x our baseline). That causes KV cache churn on a subset of GPUs and spikes per-request latencies as we rehydrate caches.

Why rollback helps: v1 uses a different kernel path and smaller working set, so it should avoid the thrashing. Rollback caveats:
- We'll need to ensure the v1 variant is loaded and warmed on the Finlytics serving pool before shifting traffic (5–10m warm).
- If the pool lacks spare capacity we may route to a different GPU pool (incurs cross-pool latency + cost).
- Monitoring: I will instrument a heatmap and watch for KV hit-rate and memory pressure during the ramp.

Recommendation: authorize the 50% -> 100% ramp to v1 with a warm-up window. I'll own the rollback operations and the technical postmortem.

—Vivek
Director, Serving Runtime
From: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.ai>

Subject: Approval request: temporary SLA carveout & routing override for Finlytics (model-3a-v2 -> v1)

Team — I'm drafting the approval we're asking from leadership and legal/procurement. Proposed ask to Finlytics and internal approvers:

- Temporary SLA carveout for Finlytics for the affected window (requested: 12 hours starting now) while we execute rollback and stabilization.
- Immediate routing override to model-3a-v1 with 50% traffic shift, ramp to 100% if metrics pass.
- Allow engineering to allocate spare capacity / cross-pool routing for warm-up and mitigation.
- Provide Finlytics a credit equal to one day of usage (TBD by finance) as gesture of goodwill contingent on RCA.

Related doc/jira: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/INF-9876, live dashboard: https://dashboard.redwood.ai/dashboards/INF-9876

Marissa / Vivek / Neha: please confirm you can execute the plan on your side. If yes, I'll ask for a (<30m) signoff from legal on the carveout and then proceed.

—Ethan
